relationships.subject: plasma adsorption
relationships.evidence_quote: During the 5 cycles of plasma adsorption therapy, proinflammatory cytokines such as IL-6 and TNF-α were found to continue declining until they reached normal levels

relationships.subject: NLRP3
relationships.evidence_quote: The activation of the Nod-like receptor pyrin domain-containing protein 3 (NLRP3) inflammasome leads to the release of IL-1β and other proinflammatory cytokines that are essential to gout pathogenesis (5).

key_findings: In a single refractory gout case, plasma adsorption lowered IL-6 and TNF-alpha to normal levels with clinical improvement of fever, swelling and pain.
No significant before/after cytokine difference was found given small sample size and fluctuation.
